requirements.evidence: Migrations match names and columns exactly (entities_slug_unique; owner_seq storedAs "case when role = 'owner' then 1 else null end" + unique entity_memberships_one_owner, create_entity_memberships_table.php:22-28). Policies match the matrix (EntityPolicy.php, EntityMembershipPolicy.php:41-52 owner never deletable, self-removal allowed). EntityPickController.php:18-27 authorizes view (403 before session write), audit log, redirect to dashboard. Members: exists:users,email (Members.php:30), duplicate -> ValidationException on email (AddMember.php:21-23), role Rule::in(manageable) (Members.php:66-68), last-manager guard (RemoveMember.php:21-23). Settings: slug unique ignoring self (Settings.php:93), delete clears session only if current (Settings.php:57-59), TransferOwnership.php:23-34 locks rows, requires admin of this entity other than caller, 403 when owner row missing, demote-then-promote in a transaction. Dashboard hides the settings link behind @can('manageSettings') (dashboard.blade.php:12-14). Both lang files carry the quoted texts; routes match the contract.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes go through new app/Actions/* classes that authorize inside (AddMember, AssignRole, RemoveMember, TransferOwnership, UpdateEntity, DeleteEntity). #[Validate] on Members::$email; Settings uses rules(), which the policy allows. #[Fillable] on both models. Reuses <x-form-field>/<x-button>. CHANGELOG and docs/database-schema.md updated. Deviations: Settings::$targetMembershipId has no validation rule (Settings.php:25), and Members::$status is a public, unvalidated and unlocked property (Members.php:32).

security.evidence: #[Locked] public Entity $entity on all three components, so the client cannot swap the entity. Every public action calls $this->authorize and the action re-authorizes through Gate::forUser. Membership IDs are resolved through $this->entity->memberships()->findOrFail (Members.php:62,73), so IDs from another entity give a 404. The transfer target is scoped to this entity's admins with lockForUpdate. Output is escaped with {{ }} everywhere. Add-member is rate-limited against e-mail probing (Members.php:46-48). The writable $status only reaches escaped output, so it has no real impact.

tests.evidence: Seven Pest files. They cover schema and index names, DB rejection of a second owner, the policy matrix via datasets, and pick (session untouched on 403, audit). Members tests include unauthorized and tamper cases (another entity's membership id, owner role, unknown role, last manager). Settings tests include entity swap ('the entity cannot be swapped from the client'), demoted owner, transfer to employee/self/foreign admin/missing target, session clearing, and both locales. Gap: no explicit test for the owner row vanishing during transfer.

simplicity.evidence: Lean models, policies and actions. Some redundancy: components authorize and then the actions re-authorize, sometimes with a different ability (Settings::save checks manageSettings, then UpdateEntity checks update). AssignRole.php:22-24 repeats the manageable-role check the component already validates. Members also checks create before AddMember checks it again.

readability.evidence: Small, focused classes with PHPDoc. Comments explain non-obvious points (demote-before-promote at TransferOwnership.php:30, NULLs and unique index at the migration lines 21-22). Naming is consistent, with no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Everything serves the task. Small extras: an add-member rate limiter with its lang key, the EntityMembershipPolicy::create ability, audit logs on role/remove/delete/transfer, and breadcrumbs. These are justified by the security policy and conventions. No onboarding, switcher, middleware or navbar work was added.

issues.explanation: Public property $targetMembershipId has no #[Validate]/rules() entry; the action handles bad IDs safely, but the Livewire policy asks for every user-input public property to be validated.
Public $status is a client-writable, unlocked flash message; it is only shown escaped, but it would be cleaner as a session flash or a #[Locked] property.
The task names a 403 when the owner row vanishes before transfer; the code handles it (TransferOwnership.php:26) but no test covers it.
Repeats the manageable-role check that Members::assignRole already validates, and throws InvalidArgumentException (a 500) if ever reached.
Double authorization with different abilities (component: manageSettings; action: update/delete) makes the effective rule harder to read, though it is safe.

review.summary: The change implements the full entity data model (with a DB-level single-owner constraint), both policies, entity pick, and the dashboard, members and settings Livewire pages. Writes go through authorizing Actions, entities are locked, client IDs are scoped and there are thorough unauthorized and tamper tests. Only minor convention gaps (an unvalidated public property, a writable status field) and small redundancies remain, so it is approvable with nits.
